record.paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
record.original_question: Classify achievement sets in ℝ², that is, sets of all subsums of absolutely convergent series in the plane, up to homeomorphism.

evidence.quote: Characterize achievement sets in R^2 up to homeomorphism.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an absolutely summable sequence $(x_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, define its achievement set (set of subsums) by
$$E(x) \;=\; \Big\{ \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \varepsilon_n x_n \;:\; (\varepsilon_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}} \in \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}} \Big\} \;\subseteq\; \mathbb{R}^2.$$
(For absolutely summable sequences each such series converges, so $E(x)$ is well defined; it is always compact.) On the real line, a classical result asserts that every such achievement set is homeomorphic to one of the following: a finite set, a finite disjoint union of nondegenerate compact intervals, a Cantor set, or a Cantorval (a set homeomorphic to the union of the standard Cantor set together with the open intervals removed at even-indexed steps of its construction).

Problem. Classify, up to homeomorphism, all sets of the form $E(x)\subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ as $(x_n)$ ranges over all absolutely summable sequences in $\mathbb{R}^2$. That is, give a complete list of homeomorphism types that arise as achievement sets of absolutely convergent series in the plane.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., on perturbations of multigeometric series in the plane and on achievement sets of series in $\mathbb{R}^2$) has produced at least seven distinct homeomorphism types and various structural results, but no complete classification of homeomorphism types of achievement sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$ is known. The problem is presented as open in current surveys and ongoing research.

status_evidence.title: Achievement Sets of Series in R^2 - Results in Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Studies achievement sets of absolutely convergent series in the plane and produces several new topological types.
status_evidence.claim: Recent research is still producing new homeomorphism types of plane achievement sets, indicating no complete classification.

status_evidence.title: Achievement sets on the plane — Perturbations of geometric and multigeometric series
status_evidence.snippet: The achievement set of perturbed multigeometric series can be one of at least seven types.
status_evidence.claim: Only a partial list of homeomorphism types is currently known in R^2.
